card.name: Dhol Cholom
card.tagline: Manipuri drum dance of the Yaoshang spring festival
card.profile: Dhol Cholom is a Manipuri (Meitei) drum dance of the Manipur valley performed during the Yaoshang festival (Manipuri Holi, in spring) and within the Lai Haraoba and Sankirtana traditions (Manipuri dance, Wikipedia). A group of male dancers sing and dance to the accompaniment of the dhol, a large drum used on religious occasions; the drumming builds gradually from soft to thunderous as the dance tempo intensifies, with acrobatic movement. In the classical Manipuri dance system, Dhol Cholom (with Duff Cholom) is grouped among the Shaiva (tandava) cholom dances.
card.insight: Dhol Cholom has no standalone English Wikipedia article; it is documented within the broader 'Manipuri dance' tradition as one of the cholom (drum/cymbal) dances alongside Pung Cholom and Kartal Cholom.
card.image_significance: The thunder-drum dance of Manipur. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — Manipur (Meitei), India.
